task.description: Root-cause diagnosis of ISS-0519: Letflow.Entities.Definitions.get_definition_by_name/2 raises Ecto.MultipleResultsError once >1 row shares `name` under a tenant. Determine REQ-225/226's actual intended semantics for 'the definition by this name' and recommend a concrete fix direction to CODE-DESIGNER.

result.note:
DEFECT CONFIRMED, and it is worse than the filing states -- a second, related invariant gap makes the single most obvious fix ('filter to status: :active') insufficient on its own.

1. get_definition_by_name/2 (lib/letflow/entities/definitions.ex:201-210) is exactly as filed: `from(e in EntityDefinition, where: e.name == ^name)` + `Repo.one/2`, no other predicate. entity_definitions' UNIQUE constraint is (tenant_id, name, logical_shape_version) (design req226 S1.3, entity_definition.ex:61), so 2+ logical_shape_versions under one name -- REQ-225/226's own explicitly intended versioning workflow (req225 design S1: 'name ... Immutable across logical-shape versions of the same entity type') -- makes Repo.one/2 raise. Confirmed real, not a guess.

2. REQ-225/226's OWN design already names this exact ambiguity and explicitly declines to resolve it: req226 design S6 OQ-3 states verbatim 'whether getDefinitionByName/2 should additionally accept a status filter ... is out of this requirement's own acceptance criteria ... and is left unresolved rather than guessed at.' So this is not an oversight bug in the sense of contradicting the design -- the design flagged the gap and ISS-0519 is that gap surfacing at runtime.

3. REQ-228's design (req228-entity-event-registration-commands.md line 335-338) already states the intended resolution for ONE call site: 'Resolve entity_type's current active EntityDefinition via get_definition_by_name/2 (REQ-226, reused unchanged) filtered to status: :active'. But the SHIPPED code (records.ex:358-372, `fetch_active_definition/2`) does NOT filter in the query -- it calls the unfiltered get_definition_by_name/2 then pattern-matches `%EntityDefinition{status: :active}` in Elixir afterward. That post-hoc pattern match happens too late: Repo.one/2 already raised before the pattern match is ever reached once 2+ rows share the name, regardless of their status. This is the confirmed crash path ISS-0519 names (Records.delete_record/2 -> fetch_active_definition/2 -> get_definition_by_name/2).

4. CRITICAL additional finding -- 'status: :active' is NOT a safe filter to add to the query as-is, because 'at most one :active row per name' is NOT currently an enforced invariant anywhere. Traced Definitions.activate_definition/4 (definitions.ex:319-339): it looks up ONE row via get_definition_by_name/2, calls Activation.activate_group/5 (REQ-203), then sets THAT row's status to :active via changeset/Repo.update. It never demotes any OTHER entity_definitions row under the same (tenant_id, name) back to :inactive. Grepped every `status: :active`/`status: :inactive` write site in lib/letflow/entities/ (definitions.ex:159 sets :inactive at insert; definitions.ex:336 sets :active at activation) -- there is no third site that ever flips a sibling row back to :inactive. So activating version 2 of 'customer' after version 1 was already active leaves BOTH rows with status: :active simultaneously in entity_definitions. Adding `where: e.status == :active` to get_definition_by_name/2's query would therefore still raise Ecto.MultipleResultsError, just one activation-call later than the current crash -- it narrows the crash window without closing it. Letflow.Repository.Activation.resolve/3 (activation.ex:148-177), by contrast, IS authoritative and safe: `artifact_activations` is a single upsert-pointer row keyed by (tenant_id, artifact_kind, artifact_name) (activation.ex:194-204 doc comment), so Repo.one/2 there can never see more than one row for a given name -- this pointer, not entity_definitions.status, is REQ-203's real 'exactly one active version' guarantee.

5. Existing test contract constrains the fix: test/letflow/entities/definitions_test.exs:196-211 calls `Definitions.get_definition_by_name("customer", schema)` immediately after `create_definition/2` with NO activation call, and asserts `{:ok, by_name}` succeeds. The row is `status: :inactive` at that point (definitions.ex:159). So get_definition_by_name/2's established contract is 'find by name regardless of status' -- filtering this specific function to status: :active would break this passing test and would also break activate_definition/4's own internal use of get_definition_by_name/2 (definitions.ex:321), which must find the row-to-be-activated BEFORE it is active.

6. Every current call site (grepped repo-wide): (a) definitions.ex:321 inside activate_definition/4 -- needs 'the version to promote', called before that version is active; (b) records.ex:359 inside fetch_active_definition/2 -- needs 'the currently active version specifically', per REQ-228's own stated (but unimplemented) filtered-to-active intent; (c) test/.../definitions_test.exs and test/.../record/projector_test.exs -- exercise the plain by-name lookup and the crash-repro respectively. No call site needs 'a specific version by logical_shape_version or artifact_version_id' today -- REQ-226/228 name no such lookup, so no third function is needed for that on current evidence.

RECOMMENDED FIX DIRECTION (two changes, not one):

A. Keep get_definition_by_name/2's existing contract ('the' row by name, independent of status -- matches its current tests and activate_definition/4's own use) but make it unambiguous under the REAL, intended multi-version condition: add `order_by: [desc: e.inserted_at, desc: e.id], limit: 1` so it deterministically resolves to the newest row by name instead of raising when 2+ rows exist. This is consistent with how every other 'latest by name' resolution in this codebase already orders (list_definitions/2's own `ORDER BY inserted_at DESC, id DESC`, req226 design S3.3 step 4) and fixes activate_definition/4's need to find 'the latest version to promote' without changing its existing tests' expected behavior (a single row still resolves to itself).

B. Add a NEW function -- e.g. `get_active_definition_by_name/2` -- for the 'currently active version' semantic REQ-228's design already named but never got implemented correctly. Implement it via Letflow.Repository.Activation.resolve/3 (the actually-authoritative pointer, item 4 above), not via entity_definitions.status: resolve(:entity, name, prefix) -> on {:ok, %ArtifactVersion{version_id: vid}}, query `where: e.name == ^name and e.artifact_version_id == ^vid` (guaranteed at most one row, since each create_definition/2 call mints one fresh artifact_version_id per row -- confirmed by req226 design S4's dedup trace: a same-name resubmission always mints a new artifact_versions row, never reuses one); on {:error, :not_activated} -> {:error, :not_found} (matching fetch_active_definition/2's own existing not-found translation, records.ex:363-367). Change Records.fetch_active_definition/2 (records.ex:358-372) to call this new function instead of get_definition_by_name/2 + a post-hoc status pattern-match, removing the now-provably-unsafe status-based branch entirely.

C. (Flag for CODE-DESIGNER to decide scope, not required to close ISS-0519's crash if B is implemented via Activation.resolve/3 rather than entity_definitions.status): activate_definition/4's failure to demote sibling rows to :inactive (item 4) is a real, separate latent bug -- entity_definitions.status can silently hold multiple simultaneous :active rows per name today, contradicting its own moduledoc's framing as a synced 'read-convenience denormalisation' of the authoritative pointer. Recommend fixing this in the same pass (have activate_definition/4 also set every OTHER entity_definitions row under (tenant_id, name) to :inactive, ideally inside the same Repo.update/transaction) so the column stops drifting from ground truth -- otherwise a future caller who (reasonably, given the column's name and moduledoc) trusts `status: :active` directly against entity_definitions instead of calling Activation.resolve/3 will get silently wrong answers (not a crash, but a correctness bug in the same family). This does not require a new migration/index; if CODE-DESIGNER wants a DB-level guarantee too, a partial unique index `UNIQUE (tenant_id, name) WHERE status = 'active'` is the natural enforcement mechanism, translated via `unique_constraint/3` the same way the existing (tenant_id, name, logical_shape_version) constraint already is (entity_definition.ex:77).
